scope: Read-only concrete next-step plan for stage13 candidate2: bounded TLS allocation-failure recovery by reclaiming only idle adaptive input slots. No source/test/tracked documentation/Git changes, builds, suite executions or board access. Deferred AAC owner-view is excluded. Numeric pool, TLS reserve, headroom and IRAM policy remain unchanged.

configuration_context.source: Existing build-c3-transfer configuration captured for this plan, not a claim about in-progress new parent firmware builds.

facts.fact: CYD uses the canonical shared adaptive queue. create rounds packet target/minimum, may succeed with fewer than target slots if the minimum is funded, and destroys only its own allocations/semaphores on constructor failure. destroy has an explicit quiescent-callers contract and no internal reader/refcount protection.

release_one already removes only IDLE data slots while resident>minimum, under the queue portMUX, and frees after unlocking. WRITING, READY, READING, ALLOCATING and caller-owned control storage are not candidates. No queue algorithm or payload eviction is needed for this port.

restore/restore_one already allocate outside the queue lock and revalidate the current limit before publishing. Only the producer restores between connections. Concurrent reclamation can leave sparse resident slot indexes; existing retirement logic ranks resident pointers, not slot index alone.

CYD startup is a CAS OFF->STARTING transaction. It creates three notification-gated tasks and completes all fallible pool/codec/output/LED operations before READY. Every failure path deletes gated tasks and destroys s_encoded, then publishes OFF last. Donor bind-at-create would expose a pool that this rollback later frees.

After successful READY, current CYD has no runtime pool-destruction/replacement API. audio_service_stop changes playback intent; maintenance parks owners but keeps pool lifetime. Health reads stats after seeing READY. Neither Stop nor a stream generation change is permission to unbind/destroy the queue.

C3 tls_input_reserve binds one atomic pointer with an application-lifetime contract. An atomic pointer load prevents a pointer data race, but cannot keep a separately destroyed object alive. Its allocator wrapper uses largest-block pre-reclaim and retry loops. Those loops are not intrinsically bounded if a producer repeatedly restores slots concurrently.

The pinned SDK6.0.2 provides esp_mbedtls_mem_calloc/free even with dynamic TLS buffers disabled. Current internal allocation maps calloc to heap_caps_calloc(INTERNAL|8BIT); platform STD_CALLOC uses this symbol. A linker wrapper is plausible without copying dynamic-RX private ABI or adding a TLS static slot.

heap_caps_register_failed_alloc_callback stores a single process-wide callback and rejects NULL; it is not a callback chain, an unregister API or an allocation-retry API. CYD native_health already owns it. The current callback can run on either core/task or ISR and deliberately performs no heap/free/logging operation. Replacing it would lose diagnostics and inserting reclamation into it would violate its context/lock contract.

recommended_bounded_candidate.name: Optional task-context esp_mbedtls_mem_calloc failure-only reclaim wrapper with explicit pool lifetime pins
recommended_bounded_candidate.feature_gate: Initially opt-in (default n). Require adaptive input, audited SDK allocator symbol/internal allocation, no custom allocator and no HEAP_ABORT_WHEN_ALLOCATION_FAILS. Keep dynamic TLS/reserve/IRAM settings and all pool sizes unchanged. Nonadaptive/option-off builds have no new wrapper/bind behavior.
recommended_bounded_candidate.allocator_entry: Use --wrap=esp_mbedtls_mem_calloc and --undefined=__wrap_esp_mbedtls_mem_calloc like the donor. No malloc/calloc/free global wrappers, no heap failed-callback registration, no mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free runtime swap, no free wrapper and no borrowed/static reserve pointers.
flow: Malformed zero/overflow arguments forward exactly once to __real_esp_mbedtls_mem_calloc before any queue/registry/counter policy. Preserve the SDK argument and return semantics; do not evict for malformed requests.

For valid arguments, call the real SDK allocator first, with no registry/queue/health locks held. A success causes no reclamation. This first bounded version deliberately does not copy the donor pre-allocation largest-block heuristic.

After a genuine NULL return, bypass reclamation in ISR context. In task context acquire a nonallocating registry pin; if unbound/detaching/refcount would overflow, return the original failure without queue access.

Read actual queue stats while pinned. Set a fixed per-call successful-release budget to initial target-minus-minimum (not resident-minus-minimum, not a while-until-largest loop). Each successful release_one consumes one budget and permits exactly one real calloc retry. Stop on success, release failure, or exhausted budget. Concurrent producer refill must not extend the budget.

Keep the lifetime pin until all queue reads/releases for this call are finished. A bounded retry may run with a pin but never with the registry or queue spinlock held. Release the pin on every return path. Do not restore, shrink a policy limit, allocate new slots, log, or wait for a consumer from the wrapper.

All returned pointers remain ordinary SDK heap pointers paired with the unchanged SDK free. Separate attempt/reclaimed/recovered metrics, if needed, are allocation-free and updated outside queue locks. Existing health allocation-failure counts still observe real failed attempts even when a later retry recovers; do not relabel those attempts as fatal stream failures.
recommended_bounded_candidate.numeric_policy: Current source requests16KiB nominal encoded budget with a minimum of4 packet allocations and target determined by packet capacity; typical current layout gives8 target slots. Reclaim at most existing idle extras above the existing4-slot floor. No new32KiB headroom, static TLS slot, reduced TLS record size, codec expansion or startup floor policy. Requested storage released is not measured usable bytes/largest-block gain.
recommended_bounded_candidate.reason_for_lifetime_pins: Binding only after successful startup already makes the current production pool application-lived. Pins make an explicit unbind contract testable and avoid silently relying on a bare atomic pointer if teardown is ever added. They do not themselves authorize a new runtime teardown feature.

bind_unbind_protocol.existing_api: Queue reclamation/restore APIs exist; a CYD registry, bind, pin/refcount, detach or unbind API does not. Donor bind has no unbind/drain.
bind_unbind_protocol.registry: A static task-context registry guarded by its own portMUX: active pointer, optional detached/retired pointer, pin count. No allocation, queue operation, SDK heap call, logging or blocking RTOS call while holding the registry lock. Bind/unbind are exclusive lifecycle-owner operations; do not claim arbitrary multiowner/ABA safety.
proposed_public_contracts: bind(input): nonallocating; reject NULL, a different active owner, or a retired owner with undrained pins. Repeated bind to the same still-active owner may be idempotent. Do not overwrite a foreign/retired pointer.

pin(): under registry lock, increment count only for an active non-detaching pointer and representable count; then release lock before touching the queue. unpin(): decrement exactly one owned pin under registry lock, with no queue/heap work inside.

unbind_try(expected): exclusive owner, checked exact pointer. First detach removes active admission and retains expected as retired. Return BUSY while pins exist; wrong owner has no effects. Return OK only after count==0 and retire record can be consumed. Keep new binds rejected during drain. A timeout/BUSY never authorizes destroy, and never restores an unchecked stale pointer.

No unbind call is needed on current playback Stop/EOF/maintenance, because the successful pipeline pool remains live. If future actual teardown is implemented, its owner must satisfy the separate queue-wide quiescence conditions below.
exact_startup_entrypoint: Leave the reclaimer unbound throughout OFF->STARTING, constructor allocations, control attachment, codec registration, gated task creation, output init and LED init. Startup OOM must remain recoverable by existing rollback without a hook into partial state.

After all fallible startup work and task tracking, perform the existing READY publication. Immediately after this commit, before the existing task-notify loop, attempt the nonallocating bind of s_encoded. No startup failure/rollback branch may occur after a published binding.

If optional binding is unexpectedly rejected, do not jump to failed after READY: keep the new pool unbound, retain original startup success and record the feature rejection outside locks. A different existing valid binding is not overwritten. The current CAS/start-once lifecycle makes such a collision a contract failure to test, not a normal allocation-failure path.

Other TLS users in the short READY-before-bind window merely use the real allocator; they cannot observe a partial pool through the registry. Pipeline tasks remain gated until notifications. Binding publishes only a fully initialized, successful application-lifetime queue.
bind_unbind_protocol.rollback: The current failed-startup path must assert/qualify that its queue was never exported to the registry; delete all still-gated tasks, then destroy queue/RTOS allocations and publish OFF last exactly as today. If a future change exports before a fallible step, it must first detach/drain all pins before destruction; moving the bind earlier is an intentional negative control, not a recommended design.
future_teardown_preconditions: Close public admission and prove all stream/decoder/other queue callers quiescent, including WRITING/READING leases, blocked semaphore users and any producer restore_one malloc in flight. destroy does not enforce or wait for these conditions.

A simple READY->OFF store alone is not enough: a health reader may have observed READY and not yet called adaptive_input_stats. Any new runtime teardown must also provide a lifetime pin/admission barrier for health and all other direct s_encoded readers, or a proven lifecycle-owner synchronization that drains them.

Detach allocator admission using the checked unbind, wait/drain outside all spinlocks, and keep the queue/control storage alive if drain times out. Only after all ordinary queue users and all allocator pins are absent may adaptive_input_destroy delete buffers/semaphores. Caller-owned control storage must outlive the queue and is never freed by queue destroy.

Do not add runtime destroy/recreate, reuse an old pointer address or introduce a new owner while a retired registry entry is draining as part of this candidate. If arbitrary owner replacement is later needed, specify checked generation tokens rather than silently broadening this exclusive-owner contract.

smp_lock_order_and_context: No nested registry->queue or queue->registry lock acquisition: pin/unpin changes registry fields only; all queue operations begin after releasing registry lock. A refcount pin is lifetime ownership, not a held spinlock.

Canonical queue lock protects slot state/resident/FIFO only. malloc/free remain outside it. Reclaimer can be called by multiple TLS tasks; queue release_one serializes slot removal, so no two wrappers free the same pointer and the existing floor is checked atomically.

Never hold registry/queue/audio-control/state/health spinlocks across the real SDK allocator, free, RTOS waits or unbind drain. The heap failure callback may acquire only the existing health lock; it must not call the reclaimer or wait on registry state.

Producer restore may overlap pressure reclaim; ALLOCATING slots and successful malloc publication use the existing queue protocol. A fixed reclaim budget ensures completion despite repeated restore. No producer or decoder task may call unbind while retaining an unaccounted queue operation or lease.

Keep new reclamation task-only; unsupported ISR entry forwards to the real allocator without registry/queue access. Do not claim IRAM/cache-disabled safety for the new task wrapper from the health callback IRAM annotation.
Preserve current core affinities: radio_stream core0 priority3, audio_decode core1 priority5, audio_output core1 priority6. This plan adds no task or IPC and does not move work between cores.

host_qualification_required_not_run.area: Actual translation units and allocator contract
host_qualification_required_not_run.positive: Compile the real shared queue and new registry/wrapper separately with real SDK esp_mem.c where feasible, explicit heap/RTOS seams; verify zero/overflow and success forward unchanged, no eviction on success, calloc zeroing and real free pairing. Distinguish seam failures from actual SDK behavior.
negative_controls: Skip or alter original successful allocator result

host_qualification_required_not_run.positive: Extend actual CYD start/gated-task fault injection at every constructor/codec/task/output/LED failure while a concurrent unrelated TLS caller attempts allocation. Verify registry never sees the failed queue, no UAF/leak, OFF retry succeeds, successful bind occurs after READY and before first notified owner runs.
negative_controls: Bind immediately after create before later failure
Notify an owner before final bind/publication boundary

host_qualification_required_not_run.positive: Use only public queue APIs to create simultaneous WRITING, READY and READING payloads plus independent control storage; checksum bytes/FIFO while TLS pressure frees IDLE extras. Verify resident>=minimum and pointer/state integrity at all times, including holes and concurrent consumer returns.

Deterministically pause a pinned wrapper before release/retry, detach on another thread, prove new pins denied and wrong-owner unbind no effect; destruction remains prohibited until all pins drain. Hold a queue restore malloc in flight to show allocator-pin drainage alone is insufficient for generic destroy.
negative_controls: Load atomic pointer without acquiring pin
Return unbind OK with pins outstanding
Allow rebind while retired owner drains

host_qualification_required_not_run.area: Bounded SMP retry and lock discipline
host_qualification_required_not_run.positive: Overlap actual producer restore, consumer traffic, multiple wrapper callers and snapshots with explicit barriers/lock-depth assertions; heap/free/log/waits forbidden inside queue/registry locks. A restoring producer can keep slots available, yet each allocation must stop after its initial fixed target-minus-minimum successful-release budget.
negative_controls: Replace fixed budget by an unbounded while-reclaim loop
Lose unpin on an early return

host_qualification_required_not_run.positive: Keep actual native_health callback registration/counters; exercise failed attempts later recovered by wrapper, ISR bypass, unbound and option-off/nonadaptive profiles, constructor OOM, reclaim exhaustion and retry failure. ASan/UBSan positives plus exact semantic mutants; sanitizer crashes/timeouts are not successful mutant detections.
negative_controls: Make optional bind collision trigger rollback after READY

actual_target_qualification_required_not: First compile whole new production queue/registry/wrapper TUs with pinned SDK6.0.2 classic Xtensa headers/config/flags; verify symbols/wrapper chain by nm/relocations and dependency/source/config/tool hashes before/after. No RISC-V evidence substituted. Test option off/default behavior and unsupported/custom/abort allocation modes fail closed or stay disabled.

Add isolated classic ESP32 QEMU two-core tests using real SDK heap_caps_calloc via public mbedtls_calloc (not only a direct wrapper call). Induce an actual observed allocator NULL with controlled internal-heap pressure, then verify reclamation/retry recovery, full zeroing, untouched nonidle payload/control bytes, unchanged floor and correct ordinary SDK free. Stop/fail if the intended failure was never observed; a largest-block estimate alone is not proof of OOM.

Use real FreeRTOS barriers/tasks on both cores for pin/detach/restore/caller overlap, bounded retry under replenishment, health-counter preservation and failed initialization. Distinct exact semantic target controls must fail named assertions; terminal uniqueness/exit/output guards and frozen input hashes bind the run. This is target heap/SMP evidence, not RF/TLS handshake or board timing proof.

After bounded helper evidence, run integrated production builds/Clang and existing startup/maintenance/queue/HTTP/pipeline regressions. Review actual final linker wrapper references, no free/static-TLS additions, task/core affinity and map resource delta. Preserve diagnostic/quiet and all3 backend configurations as appropriate.

Only then qualify real CYD simultaneous radio/HTTPS/redirect/reconnect/OTA/maintenance workloads with actual allocation failures/recoveries, internal free/largest/minimum heap, input resident/ready/reading, decoder/output failures, stack minima and driver queue/timing observations. Physical measurements gate changing default activation or any numeric pool/TLS/headroom/IRAM policy.
already_available_evidence_to_reuse: Existing adaptive-input host fixture already exercises real queue/TLS donor wrapper with 60000 concurrent packets, constructor failure, sparse idle reclaim, protected queue/leases, restore/set-limit races and independent control storage; it has no new CYD registry/unbind lifetime proof.

Existing actual CYD startup host fixture already executes notification gates and injects startup failure/rollback. It must be extended for this new publication seam; current success does not qualify an unimplemented allocator hook.
Historical M13 audit and candidate1 HTTP qualification remain separate immutable evidence. This plan is not an additional completed transfer, target build or board qualification.
out_of_scope: Deferred AAC owner-view and any investigation/repair of it
Global heap hooks or allocator replacement
open_decisions_before_implementation: Approve the failure-only first version and initially opt-in feature gate; a preallocation largest-block heuristic is deliberately separate.

Choose whether to include checked nonblocking detach/pins now or explicitly expose only application-lifetime binding with no unbind API. The recommended pinned protocol above gives a concrete safe detach seam, but adding general runtime teardown is out of scope.
